components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled, colored button in the system — reserved for the primary action on a page or panel.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary" type="button"><svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg>Add Book</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; padding: 6px 13px; min-height: 30px; font: 500 13px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, system-ui, sans-serif; color: #fff; background: var(--accent-fill, #0069D9); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 6px); box-shadow: 0 1px 1.5px rgba(0,0,0,0.10), inset 0 0.5px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.35); cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; transition: background 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 60ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--accent-hover, #0059B8); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.975); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0069D9); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 4px; } .ds-btn-primary .ds-icon { width: 16px; height: 16px; flex: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default button shape — neutral fill, hairline border. Used everywhere a primary button isn't warranted.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; padding: 6px 13px; min-height: 30px; font: 500 13px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, system-ui, sans-serif; color: var(--fg, rgba(0,0,0,0.88)); background: var(--bg-raised, #fff); border: 1px solid var(--separator-strong, rgba(0,0,0,0.18)); border-radius: var(--r-sm, 6px); box-shadow: 0 1px 1.5px rgba(0,0,0,0.10), inset 0 0.5px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.35); cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; transition: background 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 60ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--bg-hover, rgba(0,0,0,0.045)); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.975); background: var(--bg-active, rgba(0,0,0,0.075)); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0069D9); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 4px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: A rounded status pill; recolored per semantic role (accent/red/orange/green/teal) but always the same shape.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 2px 8px; font: 600 11px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.02em; border-radius: 999px; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-badge-red { background: var(--red-soft, rgba(215,0,21,0.10)); color: var(--red, #D70015); } .ds-badge-accent { background: var(--accent-soft, rgba(0,105,217,0.11)); color: var(--accent, #0069D9); } .ds-badge-green { background: var(--green-soft, rgba(30,122,56,0.11)); color: var(--green, #1E7A38); }

components.name: Stat Tile
components.description: The primary dashboard card — a linkable tile that lifts slightly on hover, colored by the metric's urgency.
components.html: Overdue4
components.css: .ds-stat { display: block; background: var(--bg-content, #fff); border-radius: var(--r-lg, 12px); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.07), 0 0 0 0.5px rgba(0,0,0,0.05); padding: 14px 16px; text-decoration: none; transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-stat:hover { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.09), 0 0 0 0.5px rgba(0,0,0,0.05); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-stat-top { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; color: var(--fg-secondary, rgba(0,0,0,0.56)); font: 500 12px -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-stat-value { display: block; font: 600 28px -apple-system, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.025em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; margin-top: 6px; } .ds-stat-red .ds-stat-value, .ds-stat-red .ds-stat-top { color: var(--red, #D70015); } .ds-icon-sm { width: 14px; height: 14px; flex: none; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: The single text-input style used across every form in the system, including selects and textareas.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 5px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { font: 500 12px inherit; color: var(--fg-secondary, rgba(0,0,0,0.56)); } .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 6px 10px; min-height: 30px; font: 13px inherit; color: var(--fg, rgba(0,0,0,0.88)); background: var(--bg-field, #fff); border: 1px solid var(--separator-strong, rgba(0,0,0,0.18)); border-radius: var(--r-sm, 6px); transition: border-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 180ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent, #0069D9); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--accent-soft, rgba(0,105,217,0.11)); }

components.name: Book Cover
components.description: Signature component: a deterministic gradient-plus-initial cover for books with no real artwork, hue-derived from ISBN.
components.css: .ds-book-cover { width: 100%; height: 68px; border-radius: var(--r-lg, 12px) var(--r-lg, 12px) 0 0; background: linear-gradient(135deg, hsl(210 55% 30%), hsl(242 55% 18%)); color: rgba(255,255,255,0.94); font: 700 26px -apple-system, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.01em; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }

components.name: Confirmation Sheet
components.description: Signature component: macOS-style modal for destructive/consequential actions, always naming the exact record.

components.css: .ds-sheet { width: min(400px, calc(100vw - 32px)); background: var(--bg-raised, #fff); border-radius: var(--r-lg, 12px); box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.20), 0 0 0 0.5px rgba(0,0,0,0.10); padding: 20px 22px 16px; text-align: center; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', sans-serif; } .ds-sheet-icon { width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 50%; display: grid; place-items: center; margin: 0 auto 12px; background: var(--red-soft, rgba(215,0,21,0.10)); color: var(--red, #D70015); } .ds-sheet-title { font: 600 15px inherit; margin: 0 0 5px; color: var(--fg, rgba(0,0,0,0.88)); } .ds-sheet-body { font: 13px inherit; color: var(--fg-secondary, rgba(0,0,0,0.56)); margin: 0; } .ds-sheet-actions { display: flex; gap: 8px; margin-top: 18px; } .ds-icon-lg { width: 20px; height: 20px; } .ds-btn-danger { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; padding: 6px 13px; min-height: 30px; font: 500 13px inherit; color: var(--red, #D70015); background: var(--bg-raised, #fff); border: 1px solid var(--separator-strong, rgba(0,0,0,0.18)); border-radius: var(--r-sm, 6px); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: var(--red-soft, rgba(215,0,21,0.10)); }

components.name: Tab Bar Item
components.description: Signature component: the member (borrower) phone shell's bottom tab, with an unread-style badge.

components.css: .ds-tab-item { flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 3px; padding: 5px 2px 4px; text-decoration: none; color: var(--fg-secondary, rgba(0,0,0,0.56)); font: 500 10px -apple-system, sans-serif; border-radius: 6px; transition: color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-tab-item:active { transform: scale(0.92); } .ds-tab-item-active { color: var(--accent, #0069D9); } .ds-tab-icon { position: relative; display: block; line-height: 0; } .ds-tab-icon svg { width: 24px; height: 24px; margin: 0 auto; } .ds-tab-badge { position: absolute; top: -4px; right: -9px; min-width: 15px; height: 15px; padding: 0 3px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--red-fill, #D70015); color: #fff; font: 700 9px -apple-system, sans-serif; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }

narrative.overview:
The interface is built around the librarian's actual desk: a source-list sidebar stands in for the shelf of collections (Dashboard, Books, Members, History), a translucent sticky toolbar holds the tools for whatever's open, and content panels behave like folders and documents — flat, hairline-bordered, quiet until you act on them. This isn't a library app wearing macOS chrome for polish; the desk metaphor is the actual information architecture. Everything native-feeling about it (traffic-light dots, SF-style type, frosted-glass overlays, sheet-style confirmations) exists to make that metaphor legible rather than as decoration for its own sake.

The system is self-contained by construction — hand-written CSS, vanilla JS, inline SVG icons, no CDN — so the desk metaphor renders identically offline and on restricted campus networks, which matters because the primary audience is a school library where that constraint is real, not aspirational.

Two sibling experiences share this system without diverging from it: the librarian's desk is desktop-only and dense; the borrower's side collapses to an iOS-style phone shell (bottom tab bar, large-title header) using the exact same tokens, just recomposed. One design system, two native-feeling shells.
keyCharacteristics: Source-list sidebar + translucent sticky toolbar as the primary navigation grammar
Flat, hairline-bordered panels; shadows are soft and ambient, never heavy
Frosted-glass translucency reserved for floating/overlay chrome (sidebar, toolbar, glass icon buttons, sheets)
A restrained accent (system blue) used only to mark selection, primary action, and links — never as page-level decoration
Full light/dark appearance parity, with every token re-tuned per mode rather than just dimmed
macOS-style confirmation sheets for anything destructive, naming the exact record being acted on

rules.name: The Text/Fill Split Rule
rules.body: Every semantic color that appears both as text-on-page and as a filled surface holding white text gets two tokens (system-blue vs. its fill variant), because a blue tuned to be legible as text in dark mode is too light to hold white text as a button fill. Never reuse the text variant as a background-with-white-text, or vice versa.

rules.name: The Independent-Mode Rule
rules.body: Dark appearance is never filter: invert() or a flat opacity dim — every single token is re-picked by hand for the dark surface it sits on, checked against the same WCAG math as light mode.

rules.name: The One-Heading Rule
rules.body: Exactly one real h1 exists per page (the toolbar title); any larger decorative title is aria-hidden and purely visual.

rules.name: The Glass-Is-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Frosted-glass blur is reserved for floating navigational/overlay chrome — sidebar, toolbar, menus, sheets, the round glass icon buttons — never for resting content surfaces.

rules.name: The No-Blur Fallback Rule
rules.body: Every backdrop-filter use ships an @supports not fallback to a flat, opaque surface color — never a transparent layer with no blur.

rules.name: The Explain-the-Block Rule
rules.body: When a control is disabled or an action is unavailable, the interface surfaces the specific reason as copy near the control rather than leaving a silently disabled button.

dos: Do keep color meaning-only: system blue for selection/primary/links, red/amber/forest/teal for status — never decorative color blocking on neutral surfaces.
Do re-derive every color independently for dark mode and verify it against real WCAG contrast math; don't dim or invert.
Do use frosted-glass blur only for floating/overlay chrome, and always ship a flat opaque @supports not fallback.
Do collapse all motion under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce — every transition and animation in this system already does.
Do keep the librarian (admin) shell desktop-only and the borrower (member) shell phone-optimized; treat them as two shells sharing one token set, not one responsive layout.
Do name the exact record in any destructive-action confirmation sheet.
donts: Don't introduce a second brand accent alongside system blue — Muted Violet exists in the token set specifically as spare semantic capacity, not an invitation to add a second "brand" color.

Don't use the fill-tuned accent token as text color, or the text-tuned token as a background holding white text — they diverge in dark mode and this mix-up has already caused real contrast bugs (breadcrumbs, tab-bar labels).
Don't add heavy drop shadows, flat Material-style colorful cards, or ripple/elevation effects — depth here is either a soft ambient hint or frosted glass, never a loud statement.
Don't disable a control without explaining why next to it.
Don't depend on a CDN, web font, icon font, or external asset for anything in this system — every icon is inline SVG and every font is a system stack, by design.
